title: Nilang .nilax manifest, format_version 2 (PROPOSED)
source_of_truth: none yet — no code emits or accepts this format
description: The manifest the ecosystem should converge on. It is published now so that every repository plans against one shape, and it is marked proposed so that no verifier rejects a v1 package for failing it. Nothing in this repository emits format_version 2. See nilax/MIGRATION.md.
deviation_from_the_plan_sketch: The ecosystem plan sketched this as a string `schemaVersion: "1.x"`. It is an integer `format_version` here, matching format_version 1, because a manifest version that is both a major line and a point release has two spellings and therefore two parsers. The plan's field coverage is otherwise carried over unchanged.

app_id.description: Reverse-DNS application identity, stable across releases.

payload.description: What the package actually carries. Declaring it explicitly is what lets a source-only bundle and a compiled artifact share one manifest without a verifier guessing which it has.

entrypoint.description: Archive-relative path of the entry file for the declared payload type.

backends.description: Backends the payload was produced by. Must be listed in compatibility/matrix.json with a status of stable or partial.

source_revision.description: Immutable identifier of the source this package was built from: a commit sha, or `sha256:<digest>` over the source tree when the build has no VCS. A value that cannot be verified to exist is refused.

runtime_abi.description: Runtime ABI the package requires. Verified against abi/runtime-abi.json; a version outside the declared compatible range is refused rather than attempted.

target.description: Single target identifier, declared in abi/runtime-abi.json.

capabilities.description: Requested capabilities, canonical lowercase. Every entry must appear in capabilities/vocabulary.json.

payload_checksums.description: Digest per payload file. This is the field that makes per-file integrity checkable by a verifier that has no signature yet, and it is what a store re-checks on repack.

signature.description: Optional at rest, required to publish. A verifier configured to require trust refuses a package whose signature is absent.

signed_fields.description: The manifest fields covered by the signature, in canonical order. See signing/signing.json; the list is explicit so that adding a field cannot silently fall outside or inside the signature.
